title: Reduction Trace Equivalence

basis.scope: Canonical reduction trace equivalence and canonical trace normalization for REDUCE_025 outputs, including outcome-preserving comparison, trace identity distinction, and comparison-class invariants.

core_rule.statement: Trace equivalence is diagnostic only; equivalent traces preserve lawful reduction semantics, identical canonical outcomes, and halt classification; trace identity is stronger than equivalence; canonical trace normalization produces TNF(Trace); RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define when two reduction traces are considered equivalent despite differing reduction paths, provided they preserve lawful continuation semantics and identical reduction outcomes.

canonical_claims.statement: Equivalent traces preserve lawful reduction semantics and identical canonical outcomes.
Canonical trace normalization produces TNF(Trace) without modifying reduction semantics.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Trace Equivalence
formal_objects.definition: An equivalence relation over reduction traces that identifies traces which originate from the same input continuation, preserve lawful reduction semantics, preserve equivalent continuation behavior, terminate in the same canonical outcome, and preserve halt classification.

formal_objects.name: Canonical Trace Form
formal_objects.definition: A normalized representative of a reduction trace used for outcome-preserving comparison. It preserves evaluation order, removes implementation-specific metadata, retains canonical reduction events, and normalizes step numbering and halt classification without altering reduction semantics.

equivalence_classes.description: Equivalent traces terminating in the same canonical normal form.
Equivalent traces terminating in the same partial normal form.
Equivalent traces terminating in the same classified continuation failure.

comparison_rules: Equivalent traces must originate from the same continuation expression.
Equivalent traces must preserve process equivalence.
Equivalent traces may differ in intermediate reduction ordering where lawful.
Equivalent traces must terminate in the same reduction outcome.
Equivalent traces must preserve failure taxonomy.
invariants: Trace equivalence does not imply trace identity.
